body: based on my limited Rust knowledge, it seems that we need to return a `String` rather than an `&str` here otherwise there would be a dangling reference to the file contents which is local to this function. The other nearby functions are modified to return `Option<String>` rather than `Option<&str>` accordingly.
https://hatch.pypa.io/1.9/version/#configuration
https://hatch.pypa.io/1.9/version/#configuration
https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/single-source-version/#build-system-version-handling
passing through the context allows us to use `context.current_dir` to access files referenced by `pyproject.toml` above

the codecov warning seems erroneous, these lines are used where we pass `"src/__init__.py"` to `file_path` in `test_extract_pep621_dynamic_version_hatchling_1`, as can be observed by commenting out these lines to make the test fail.
this could be a follow-up PR as the regex option seems rather niche
other build backends could also be separate PRs
This module is not python-specific so the function naming should reflect that.
Please reference relevant documentation in comments as appropriate .
Since this is parsing Python files please validate any returned value via `semver::Version::parse`
I opted for https://docs.rs/pep440_rs/latest/pep440_rs/index.html instead as the `semver` crate seemed undesirably restrictive on allowed syntax. Let me know if that is okay!
Wait I picked the wrong crate from our dependencies, `versions::Version::new` (or `versions::Mess::new`) should be flexible enough to handle everything.

> Wait I picked the wrong crate from our dependencies, `versions::Version::new` (or `versions::Mess::new`) should be flexible enough to handle everything.

changed to `versions::Version::new`!

You changed it to `Versioning` which may end up falling back to `Mess`; I would prefer avoiding going through multiple fallbacks during validation (e.g. just using `Mess` straight away). Since `Mess` looks very loose, I feel like `Version` is a sensible choice to ensure a higher level of sanity, though I am not sure how messy python version strings get in practice.
let's give `Version` a go!

diff_hunk:
@@ -88,25 +90,75 @@ fn get_jsr_package_version(context: &Context, config: &PackageConfig) -> Option<
     format_version(raw_version, config.version_format)
 }
 
-fn get_poetry_version(pyproject: &toml::Table) -> Option<&str> {
+fn get_poetry_version(pyproject: &toml::Table) -> Option<String> {
     pyproject
         .get("tool")?
         .get("poetry")?
         .get("version")?
         .as_str()
+        .map(|s| s.to_owned())
 }
 
-fn get_pep621_version(pyproject: &toml::Table) -> Option<&str> {
-    pyproject.get("project")?.get("version")?.as_str()
+fn parse_file_version_for_hatchling(context: &Context, path: &str) -> Option<String> {
+    let file_contents = read_file(context.current_dir.join(path)).ok()?;
+    // https://hatch.pypa.io/latest/version/
+    let re = Regex::new(r#"(__version__|VERSION)\s*=\s*["']([^"']+)["']"#).ok()?;
+    Some(
+        re.captures(&file_contents)
+            .and_then(|cap| cap.get(2))?
+            .as_str()
+            .to_owned(),
+    )
+}
+
+fn parse_hatchling_dynamic_version(context: &Context, pyproject: &toml::Table) -> Option<String> {
+    let version_path = pyproject
+        .get("tool")?
+        .get("hatch")?
+        .get("version")?
+        .get("path")?
+        .as_str()?;
+
+    parse_file_version_for_hatchling(context, version_path)
+        .and_then(|s| Version::new(s.as_str()))
+        .map(|v| v.to_string())
